newsitem.title: UK: Clarke says George has toned down monetary advice.
newsitem.headline: Clarke says George has toned down monetary advice.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said Bank of England Governor Eddie George had toned down his advice on monetary policy since the December 11 monetary meeting.
"The Governor has actually slightly modified and toned down his advice since the December meeting," he told ITN.
"We're one quarter of one percent apart."

"Between us we've delivered the best inflation record this country has had for the last 50 years," he added. "Low inflation is going to be part of this recovery for the indefinite future as long as we keep with the Conservative government."
Clarke said he had already raised interest rates when he felt he had to and at a time when no-one had been predicting it.
"I'd put interest rates up now if I thought it was economic and the right thing to do," he added.
Referring to a call by Tim Congdon, one of the Treasury's independnet economic advisers, for a half-point rate rise, Clarke said he understood that four of his six advisers backed his own stance.
